item.title: 7 Best Single-Player FPS Games With Perfect Gunplay, Ranked
item.description:
An FPS game doesn't need flawless gunplay to achieve greatness, but it certainly helps. The recoil animation, sound design, hit reactions, weight, and responsiveness all combine to define a game's gunfeel ​​​​​, and when they all hit the mark, you get something truly magical. Even if the rest of the campaign consists of nothing but awfulness, a shooter might still be worth playing if it feels amazing to fire a pistol, an SMG, or (most importantly) a shotgun.

For this article, let's just focus on the heart and soul of first-person shooters. These are excellent games to throw on when you want to blast something in the face and feel like a badass while doing it. While I wouldn't necessarily include all these titles in a "best FPS games" discussion, they are all fairly complete packages, even if their gunplay far exceeds everything else.

For the sake of variety and novelty, I'm going to cover both AAA and indie releases.

7 Selaco Wants Each Bullet To Matter

Gunfeel Isn't Just About The Act Of Firing A Gun

Let's start with perhaps a surprising pick, especially since Selaco has yet to leave early access. Built by Altered Orbit Studios on a heavily modified version of GZDoom, this indie darling smashes the environmental violence of F.E.A.R. with modern immersive sim pacing and voxel graphics, creating a symphony of destruction that makes even missed bullets feel impactful .

Every shot leaves an impact, be it the (now dead) enemies or the surrounding environment that has been reduced to fragments of drywall, ceramic tiles, and glass. Gunfeel isn't solely defined by how good it feels to pull the trigger, but also by what happens after the bullet leaves the chamber. Selaco ensures everything that comes together creates a deeply satisfying and intense onslaught of violence.

6 Metro Exodus Feels Perfect Without Making Each Gun Feel Great

Friction Enhances Gunfeel In The Right Game

Admittedly, I have a bias for fast-paced, aggressive shooters, and most of this article's picks fall under that bracket; however, Metro Exodus serves as a prime example of the exact opposite. Similar to the S.T.A.L.K.E.R. series, 4A Games' trilogy treats its guns like improvised weapons cobbled together from scrap . They are heavy, show wear and tear, and can be downright visceral.

If you enjoy twitch-reflex gameplay (and I know that I do), you aren't going to get that from Metro Exodus . The game, in general, moves at a slow, purposeful pace, and that extends to the guns and your control over them. Weapons are subject to inertia and drag, forcing you to be deliberate in your actions rather than rely on quick hip-fire blasts. The audio design is also top-notch, making each weapon sound loud, dangerous, and frankly ugly.

5 Near-Perfect Single-Player FPS Games Nobody Played

An FPS game being great is not enough. These first-person shooters are all fantastic, but they couldn't get anybody to play them.

12
By Mark Sammut

5 Severed Steel Marries Gunplay And Movement Perfectly

A Modern FPS Great That Removes One Of The Genre's Staples

Greylock Studio has quietly established itself as one of the most exciting FPS studios of the 2020s, with both of its games qualifying for this discussion. As awesome as Echo Point Nova 's open-endedness is, Severed Steel 's straight-shot level design facilitates a more hectic and consistent experience, one that blends movement and gunplay to near perfection.

The 2021 game has multiple hooks, but its biggest one is the fact that its one-armed protagonist cannot physically reload any gun; consequently, an empty pistol becomes a projectile that you toss before picking up another weapon dropped by enemies. Without the need to reload, Severed Steel eliminates the downtime found in nearly every FPS , while still retaining the tension of knowing that you might be on the verge of being largely defenseless.

Guns are snappy and destructive on their own, but they are significantly elevated by the game's movement options. Severed Steel wants players to be sliding, diving, and wall-running all over the place, activating bullet time in the process. Pulling off stunts feels so good on a basic level.

4 DOOM Eternal Makes Killing Demons Feel Incredible

The Doomguy Knows What He Is Doing, And You Are Them

Of course, Doom belongs in any discussion about gunplay; frankly, half of the franchise could fit this topic, and I imagine not everyone would go with Doom Eternal over Doom (both the original and 2016). Except for maybe Doom 3 , id Software has never prioritized making guns feel real, and that's 100% a good thing from my perspective. Doom games are, ultimately, power fantasies that cast you as a hell-destroying force of nature that turns demons into puddles of blood. Real-world ballistics have no place here.

Putting aside the platforming and limited ammo, which are divisive, Doom Eternal 's guns feel absurdly good. Simultaneously overwhelmingly powerful and completely precise, they fire when you want and how you want, with zero input latency and the freedom to quickly swap between weapons. Doom Eternal bombards players with constant threats and noise; constant smart movement is required to survive. While everything around you tries to kill you, you can always rely on your guns to do exactly what you expect from them.

10 Best Linear FPS Games For Players Exhausted Of Open-Worlds

If another open-world game sounds like an exhausting proposal, these linear FPS campaigns are short, sweet, and immensely satisfying.

6
By Ollie Tuscarny

3 RoboCop: Rogue City Does Justice To A Legend

Who Needs An SMG Or Shotgun When You Have The Auto-9?

Maybe I'm slightly overrating this one because I recently replayed it, but RoboCop: Rogue City might have the best-feeling handgun in video game history . As the starting weapon most shooters discard at the first opportunity, pistols are what you shoot when you run out of ammo for the gun you actually want to use. However, the Auto-9 doesn't play second fiddle to any shotgun or rifle , even though Rogue City has a strong arsenal of weapons beyond the iconic handgun.

Pull the trigger to unleash a three-round burst that sounds heavy, metallic, and thunderous, and RoboCop's green holographic targeting ensures that shots hit their mark. You can also remove all the UI from the screen if you want no distractions, and the gunplay somehow becomes even better. Each shot causes the Auto-9 to kick back violently, just because the cartridge is so powerful that even a supercop cannot fully control the recoil.

More Games

2 Titanfall 2 Does The Impossible

Swift Movement And Heavy Guns Shouldn't Work This Well

At the end of October 2026, Titanfall 2 officially becomes 10 years old, making the non-existence of a true sequel all that more depressing. We are never getting Titanfall 3 , are we?

Respawn knows a thing or two about crafting FPS games that nail their moment-by-moment gameplay, and Titanfall 2 is the developer's crowning achievement. Typically, a gun can either be heavy or quick, not both; however, somehow, Respawn managed to make its weapons achieve the impossible. Titanfall 2 's weapons are punchy without wrecking the momentum of the fast-as-heck parkour system , allowing everything to come together to create a seamless whole. It's kind of similar to Severed Steel , albeit with AAA production.

Titanfall 2 doesn't want you to hide behind cover and fire from a safe distance. No, you need to be constantly on the move and executing wall-runs and slides, so the gunplay doesn't punish you for playing the game how it is meant to be.

1 Trepang2 Turns You Into A Catastrophe

Now, This Is How An FPS Game Should Feel (Some Of The Time)

Another modern shooter inspired by F.E.A.R. , Trepang2 casts you as a superpowered soldier capable of extraordinary feats, and that's exactly who you become while unloading dual SMGs on an army of mercs in slow motion. Every shot is a cataclysmic event , one that sends shockwaves across the environment and back into your hands. You just barely maintain control of the guns, bullets shred enemies into blood-soaked confetti, and firing weapons can become disorienting.

Just to be clear, I mean all of the above as a complement. Trepang2 has the best gunplay out of any FPS game ever, at least for those craving high-octane madness that wants carnage rather than tactics (although you can still use some tactics). Honestly, the gunplay can be straight-up exhausting, but it's one heck of a thrill.

item.title: Over the Hill: How to Earn Pebbles Fast
item.description:
Over the Hill gives you a whole lot of rough terrain, and your starting vehicle won't always be enough to get you through it. Better upgrades can make a big difference when you are dealing with steep hills and deep mud. But before you can improve your ride, you will need Pebbles, the game's main currency. Keeping that in mind, we will share some easy ways to earn more Pebbles in Over the Hill below.

Best Cozy Games for Quick Hit Play

Players looking for a great way to wind down need to look no further than cozy games. The titles on this list are the perfect blend of cozy and quick.

By Colin Tanner

How to Get Pebbles in Over the Hill

There are multiple easy ways to earn Pebbles in Over the Hill:

Extract Meteorites

In my experience, extracting meteorites is one of the best ways to earn Pebbles in this driving game. Each region has around two or three meteorites that you can extract for rewards. You might come across them while exploring, but if you want to find them faster, you can buy a Meteor Radar from the mechanic. It points you toward a meteorite's location. Once you find one, use your winch to pull it out and collect your Pebbles.

Discover Points of Interests

Exploring the map is another simple way to earn Pebbles. You will discover different points of interest in each region, including cabins and crates. Discovering them rewards you with Pebbles. Cabins are particularly useful because reaching one reveals nearby points of interest on your map.

Photograph Wildlife

Taking pictures of wildlife is another way to earn Pebbles in this off-road driving game. Keep an eye out for animals while driving. When you find one, open the radial menu and select the camera to take its picture.

Remember that you only get Pebbles for photographing each species for the first time. Taking more pictures of the same animal won't earn you any extra currency.

Complete Challenge Trails and Recoveries

Challenge Trails are driving challenges that ask you to follow a set route and reach the finish line. Some can be tricky, with swamps, narrow paths, and steep climbs standing between you and the finish. Still, completing them earns you Pebbles and other rewards, including cosmetics.

Recoveries are another way to earn Pebbles. These missions ask you to find stranded vehicles and tow them to their recovery point. For them, you should look for a question mark icon on your map, then go there to find the vehicle. Use your winch to attach to it and tow it to the marked destination. Completing them can earn you a decent amount of Pebbles.

item.title: All Stranded Puzzle Codes & Yellow Crate Locations in Modern Warfare 4 (Time to Crate Achievement)
item.description:
Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 brings Open Combat Missions back, but only for one portion of the game's Campaign. In the Stranded mission, players must gear up to take down the North Korean forces following their invasion of South Korea. To complete the Time to Crate Achievement, you must open a total of 26 Yellow Supply Crates, some of which require codes obtained by solving puzzles. Here is every Stranded puzzle code and Yellow Crate location in Modern Warfare 4 .

Following Orders Contraband & Note Locations In Modern Warfare 4 (No Stone Unturned & No Harm Done Trophy Guide)

Following Orders has several notes, contraband items, and a code that players need to find for the No Stone Unturned Achievement in Modern Warfare 4.

By Nathan Round

All Stranded Puzzle Code Solutions in Modern Warfare 4

All Stranded Yellow Crate Locations in Modern Warfare 4

Here I have provided a map of 20 total Yellow Crates. The missing 6 can each be found in the above Shipping Containers and Bunkers, minus the Base Camp Container and Farm Field Bunker. Almost all Yellow Supply Crates can be found in fixed locations, and their locations will often be revealed to you as you clear Outposts and gather the Intel in each one.

However, a few do not spawn in a fixed location and require puzzles to find. See below for a rundown of how to get to the harder to reach Yellow Supply Crates. As for the others, refer to the map above for their locations.

Radio Tower Yellow Crate (639, 165)

To get the Radio Tower Yellow Crate, head over to the co-ordinates: 639, 165, just by the Base Camp Container. Here, climb all the way to the very top of the tower to find the Yellow Crate and a few notes along the way.

Sewer Yellow Crate (641, 164)

For this Yellow Crate, proceed to the coordinates 641, 164. Here, you can find a blue building leading down to a sewer. Head down, and you should find a crate behind a locked gate. Head right, and you will find a tunnel with a board displaying arrows. Your goal is to use these arrows to navigate the tunnel and avoid traps. Here are the directions:

  1. First Tunnel: Forward, right, forward, forward, left, left.
  2. Second Tunnel: Forward, right, forward, left, forward, left, left, down.

At the end of the second tunnel, you will reach the other side of the gate, allowing you to get the Yellow Crate.

Train Track Yellow Crate (648, 192)

To get to this Yellow Crate, head down to the train track on the south side of the map at the following co-ordinates: 648, 192. Here you can find it on a small water tower. Climb up it via the pipe to get to it.

Train Yellow Crate

This next Yellow Crate can be found on the train that periodically moves along the tracks on the south side of the map (see the map above for reference). Simply wait for the train to appear, then hop onto it to open the crate.

Cargo Truck Yellow Crate (671, 141)

This crate can be found on a Cargo Truck that will patrol around the Infantry Checkpoint #3 Outpost ( co-ordinates: 671, 141 ). Head here and hop onto the back of the truck to get to it.

Trip Wire Trapped Building Yellow Crate (606, 114)

This final crate can be found in a rigged building on the far north-east side of the map (co-ordinates: 606, 114). To get to the crate you must avoid several trip wires. You can avoid the first few at the main entrance by jumping over them and defusing those you are able to access.

The crate is found in the room to your left, though you will need to throw an explosive inside to set off the traps in order to get it.

This final crate can be found in a rigged building on the far north-east side of the map (co-ordinates: 606, 114). To get to the crate you must avoid several trip wires. You can avoid the first few at the main entrance by jumping over them and defusing those you are able to access.

The crate is found in the room to your left, though you will need to throw an explosive inside to set off the traps in order to get it.

item.title: Star Wars: Galactic Racer Just Did What Mario Kart Won't
item.description:
Mario Kart is an all-time favorite franchise for many, and it is proof that racing games don’t really have to be insanely difficult to be entertaining. Of course, this doesn’t mean that every mode is a walk in the park, but even those who are not particularly skilled can easily have a great time, which definitely does Mario Kart a favor when it comes to growing its audience. It's a formula that has worked well for the franchise, but that doesn't necessarily mean Star Wars: Galactic Racer has to follow in its footsteps.

With that being said, Star Wars: Galactic Racer has decided to put a much bigger emphasis on the consequences of failing or improving one’s skills. This generally makes any victory feel more rewarding, and it is definitely an interesting direction, considering that modern arcade racers usually prioritize immediate entertainment over punishing mistakes

Brand New Star Wars Game Is the First of Its Kind in 23 Years

Star Wars Galactic Racer brings high-speed competition back to the franchise and marks its first racer in 23 years after its TGA 2025 reveal.

By Josh Cotts

Star Wars: Galactic Racer Makes Losing More Than a Temporary Setback

No matter how great life is, everyone loses at Mario Kart at one point or another. It can certainly be frustrating, especially when the opponent suddenly gains speed right before the finish line, but at least losing doesn’t mean starting your entire progression all over again. Well, except when it comes to Knockout Tour, since it features eliminations that can actually bring your run to an early end. However, nothing in Mario Kart can lead to consequences as serious as failing in Star Wars: Galactic Racer . For example, if a player crashes too many times, this may end the entire tour, forcing everyone to regroup and start another tour. So even a small mistake could raise the stakes, which actually has the potential to make every win feel a lot more rewarding.

Moreover, although being fast is obviously important, Star Wars: Galactic Racer expects players to also understand the strengths and weaknesses of their vehicles as well. There are several classes of repulsorcraft, and each one of them has its own characteristics that people have to be aware of if they want to win. To give an example, speeder bikes can use Kinetic Burst to gain additional speed, but doing so makes them a lot more difficult to control. On the other hand, Podracers require a fine balance between speed and the use of air brakes, which can slow them down quite a lot. In other words, mastering one vehicle does not mean that players should stop trying to take their skills to the next level, which is all the more reason for victories to feel so great.

Roguelike Progression Gives Galactic Racer a Different Kind of Challenge

Star Wars: Galactic Racer also incorporates roguelike progression into its campaign, which allows players to choose between different events and routes. This means that their decisions extend beyond the track and what happens there. Without a doubt, this adds one more layer of complexity that makes the experience matter much more than most people are used to.

Star Wars: Galactic Racer features races across several planets in the Outer Rim, including Jakku and Ando Prime.

Additionally, vehicles can be customized with different parts, which can change their characteristics significantly and even provide more abilities. Some upgrades can carry over between attempts, so players won’t lose everything every time they lose. So it’s a good idea for people to really think about their builds, which is definitely a breath of fresh air in a world of traditional arcade racers.

Galactic Racer Doesn't Need to Beat Mario Kart to Prove Its Point

It’s important to note that although many might consider Galactic Racer ’s approach a refreshing change, this doesn’t mean that it necessarily has to outperform Mario Kart . To be fair, the two games might not even be targeting exactly the same audience, even though they both belong to the arcade racing genre. They generally prioritize different experiences, with Mario Kart mostly focusing on emphasizing accessible multiplayer fun. In contrast, we have Galactic Racer that is all about long-term improvement, which, if we have to be honest, is just not everyone’s cup of tea. On the other hand, not everybody who wants to play Star Wars: Galactic Racer will be required to commit to its campaign.

Star Wars: Galactic Racer Just Did What Mario Kart Won't

Star Wars Galactic Racer: All Parts & Effects
Star Wars Galactic Racer: All Currencies & How to Get Them

The game has other modes as well, including Arcade, Scenario, and competitive multiplayer modes, which is generally a strategy that aims to offer more flexibility when it comes to how people can experience its racing. These additional modes could make the game’s demanding mechanics more approachable without necessarily making the entire game significantly easier. This is a great example of how a title can compromise without actually having to compromise. Moreover, not every racing game is obliged to make winning equally achievable for everyone, and there’s certainly room in the genre for games like Galactic Racer . Maybe it could even prove that making victory harder to achieve is the better approach after all, because the challenge is exactly what makes most achievements meaningful and enjoyable.

9 /10

item.title: Monopoly GO: Radio Response Rewards and Milestones (Oct 18-21)
item.description:

Radio Response runs from October 18 to October 21 . You will have three days to work through its milestones and earn dice, Treasures tokens, and other rewards. Here's the complete list of Radio Response Monopoly GO milestones and rewards.

Why Radio Response Matters for Ghostbuster Treasures

The best part of Radio Response is that it gives you tokens for Ghostbuster Treasures. You can collect 199 tokens in total and use them to break tiles and find hidden treasures. The final reward for Ghostbuster Treasures includes a Swap Pack, 2,000 dice rolls, and a Candy Box . It will run for three days and end at the same time as Radio Response. Since it is the only banner event running alongside the dig event, make sure to collect as many rewards as you can while it's active.

Apart from the tokens, Radio Response also gives you dice rolls, a few lower-tier sticker packs, and boosters like Cash Boost and Builder's Bash. These are useful too, but the Ghostbuster Treasures tokens are the main reason to play this event.

Best Strategy for Radio Response Monopoly GO

Land on Utility and Tax Tiles

Your main goal during Radio Response should be to collect as many tokens for Ghostbuster Treasures as possible. You can earn points by landing on Tax and Utility tiles , with each landing giving you four points multiplied by your dice multiplier. Keep an eye on how far you are from these tiles and adjust your multiplier accordingly. Use a low multiplier when they are far away. On the other hand, consider increasing it when you're getting closer. This will help you earn more points without wasting too many dice on rolls that don't get you anywhere.

If you are mainly playing Radio Response to finish Ghostbuster Treasures, you can aim to stop around milestone 41 . Some of the later milestones can be harder to reach and may require you to spend a lot more dice. By milestone 41, you should have collected a decent number of tokens to use in the digging event.

Lastly, check which Flash events are active each day while Radio Response is running. You should try to play during these periods to make the most of your dice and earn more rewards.

Both Radio Response and Ghostbuster Treasures will only be available for three days, so make the most of that time.

Radio Response Monopoly GO FAQs

How many Ghostbuster Treasures tokens can you get from Radio Response?

The Radio Response event offers 199 Ghostbuster Treasure tokens in total.

How many dice rolls can you get from Radio Response?

Radio Response offers 18,215 dice rolls in total. The final milestone rewards you with 5,000 dice.

How can I get more tokens for Ghostbuster Treasures?

You can get more tokens by completing your Quick Wins, claiming free shop gifts, and reaching milestones in the tournament.

How many points do I need to complete Radio Response Monopoly GO?

You need 51,625 points to reach all 62 milestones and collect every reward.
